subject.title: RFC: Per-session tool policies — bridging operator scopes and agent tool access

question: Should Gateway operator scopes become an input to agent tool-policy resolution, and if so where should the durable scope-aware policy contract live?
rationale: The choice defines an authorization boundary across Gateway auth, agent tool filtering, config precedence, and multi-user trust semantics, so automation should not choose the guarantee or default behavior.

options.title: Design Scope-Aware Tool Policy
options.body: Keep this issue open and approve a typed `toolsByScope` or equivalent contract with enforcement layer, precedence rules, docs, and upgrade behavior before implementation.

options.title: Use Existing Session And Sender Primitives
options.body: Route the need through `toolsBySender`, group policy, session envelopes, conversation identity modes, or tenant RBAC instead of adding operator-scope-keyed config.

options.title: Decline Scope-Based RBAC
options.body: Document operator scopes as control-plane only and direct stronger multi-user isolation to separate Gateways or the broader tenant RBAC design.

recommendation.title: Design Scope-Aware Tool Policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and approve a typed `toolsByScope` or equivalent contract with enforcement layer, precedence rules, docs, and upgrade behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is the scoped conversation capability foundation plus Gateway trust-model documentation that frame this boundary.
